Summary proposal (high level):
- Phase A (EU onshore activation): provision dedicated EU tenancy + KMS integration; ingest partitioning and KV prefix caching enabled. Target pilot cutover: 6 weeks from sign-off.
- Phase B (APAC standby): warm standby nodes in APAC with auto-failover trigger policies; cold-warm warmup for critical models to reduce RTO. Can enable as an add-on post-EU go-live (2–4 week ramp).
- Failover profile: recommend conservative RTO objective of ~60–90s for full client-visible switchover (depends on session affinity and KV cache hit rate). We can quantify tighter targets after a runbook dry-run.

Term and pricing (initial options):
- 24-month commit: includes reduced unit pricing, 20% discount on standby capacity and 30% credit for professional services cutover (recommended if you want predictable pricing).
- 12-month commit: higher per-unit pricing and professional services billed up-front.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick technical sync with Karthik's team to validate RTO and cutover mechanics (I cc'd him).
2) Pricing confirmation from Mina and optional DocuSign for the 24-month proposal.
3) Share updated SOW with your procurement/legal; we can add explicit audit evidence clauses and runbook attachments.

Samantha / Dylan — quick technical notes from the infra side based on MedCore's workbook:

- RTO baseline: 60s realistic if (a) session affinity can be relaxed or (b) we warm KV caches for top-20 session prefixes. If you need sticky sessions to persist state across regions, RTO becomes 3–5min unless we replicate KV state synchronously.
- Cache strategy: recommend prefix-level KV caching + prefix-based routing to EU nodes post-cutover; this lets us avoid full model cache evictions.
- Dual-write caveat: true cross-region dual-write for stateful user metadata imposes consistency tradeoffs. For regulated PII, we recommend asymmetric dual-write with eventual convergence and explicit reconciliation windows.
- Cutover window: we can do a rolling cutover with per-region traffic ramps (5–10 minute ramps per shard). Expect a brief elevation in token latency during final KV warm-up (~10–30s spikes).
- Canary suggestion: 48-hour canary in EU with progressive traffic shifts and synthetic load tests. We'll run a dry-run at the end of the canary to validate runbook steps.

Operational links: EU cutover runbook (internal): https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/eu-cutover (we'll export a sanitized version for MedCore).

Happy to deep-dive in the 10am PT session. I'll bring a checklist that maps runbook steps to audit evidence items (KMS logs, node locality, retention).

—Karthik
Head of Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
